issues.body:
The new text added by this PR says the build 'enables the native capabilities promised by the desktop release: HDT import, SERVICE federation, ODRL policy previews, and SHACL-derived forms.' About 20 lines below, in the same comment block for the same step, the pre-existing sq-3w29b paragraph is still untouched and reads: 'release bundles explicitly enable the native HDT importer, federated SERVICE client, and ODRL policy tool. These native capabilities stay off for lean development builds; Forms remains opt-in until a release explicitly selects its larger SHACL model stack.'

The second half is now false: this release DOES explicitly select forms, and the enabled set is enumerated twice with two different memberships. A reader of the step gets two contradictory statements about whether the shipped installer contains the forms bridge or its rebuild stub. release.yml is tag-only, so nothing else corrects the reader before a real tag.

This was raised in round 4 and is unchanged.
issues.fix_hint:
Rewrite the sq-3w29b paragraph to match reality and delete the now-duplicated enumeration so the block states the feature set exactly once, e.g.:

    # [SONNET-4.6] sq-3w29b: release bundles explicitly enable the native HDT importer,
    # federated SERVICE client, ODRL policy tool, and SHACL-derived forms bridge. All four
    # stay OFF for lean development builds; the release opts in deliberately (sq-b1hdb).
issues.title: Unaddressed from round 4: the step comment now contradicts itself about whether the release enables forms

issues.body:
The step asserts only the ABSENCE of 'rebuild (the )?desktop app with'. I re-confirmed all four current stubs match, so the guard is correct today and is not vacuous in principle (in a lean build the stub fns stay reachable from their registered Tauri commands, so the literals survive into .rodata even under lto=true).

But nothing mechanically ties the four source strings to this regex. If any stub is reworded (engine.rs:347, federation.rs:66, odrl.rs:221, forms.rs:89), or a fifth optional capability lands with different wording, or a stub message becomes non-literal via format!, the grep finds nothing and the step passes green while the stub ships. Because release.yml is tag-triggered, that drift never surfaces on a PR — it surfaces as a silently degraded installer. The added comment naming the four files helps a human but enforces nothing.

Raised in rounds 3 and 4; unchanged.
issues.fix_hint:
Add a POSITIVE control in the PR-visible lane so the two checks are a matched pair. In gui.yml's tauri-build job, after the default-feature `cargo build`:

    - name: Sentinel present in lean build (guards release.yml's capability check)
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        LC_ALL=C grep -aEq 'rebuild (the )?desktop app with' target/debug/sparq-gui \
          || { echo 'stub wording drifted; release.yml capability grep is now vacuous' >&2; exit 1; }

Then a reword turns the PR lane red instead of silently disarming the tag-time guard.
issues.title: Unaddressed from round 4: the capability guard is negative-only, so a stub reword silently disarms it

issues.body:
The new step runs `grep -aEq "rebuild (the )?desktop app with" "$binary"` with the runner's inherited locale (UTF-8 on GitHub runners). A linked release binary is full of byte sequences that are invalid UTF-8. GNU grep (the Linux rows) tolerates this, but BSD grep — what `shell: bash` resolves to on macos-14 and macos-15-intel — is documented to behave unreliably on files containing invalid multibyte sequences in a UTF-8 locale, and can return 'no match' rather than scanning the whole file.

If that happens the guard is VACUOUS on those two rows: it reports success and a stub-contaminated .dmg is staged and uploaded. This is bounded — macOS/Windows rows are soft: true (release.yml:305-307), so they are non-blocking and their absence is tolerated — which is why this is minor and not major. But a guard whose whole purpose is to catch a silent degradation should not itself be able to fail silently, and the fix is one token.

Not raised in prior rounds.
issues.fix_hint:
Force the byte-oriented C locale on the scan (and, if you want, make the no-match path explicit):

          echo "Checking native capabilities in $binary"
          if LC_ALL=C grep -aEq "rebuild (the )?desktop app with" "$binary"; then
            echo "ERROR: release binary contains a native-capability rebuild stub" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: no rebuild-stub sentinel found in $binary"

Apply the same LC_ALL=C to the positive control suggested above so both halves scan identically.
issues.title: The binary grep does not force LC_ALL=C, so it can silently fail to match on the macOS rows

issues.body:
The amended bullet reads: 'The native capability feature set (`hdt,federation,odrl,forms`) is clippied and tested in debug mode by gui.yml's ADVISORY (non-gating) tauri-build job. ... the combined-state tests exercise the federation, ODRL, and forms paths.' The prior version said 'tested in debug mode on Linux'.

In gui.yml the union clippy now runs on all five rows (the `if: runner.os == 'Linux'` guard was removed) and each individual feature gets its own clippy+test on all rows, so 'clippied and tested' is substantively true. But the combined-state test still carries `if: runner.os == 'Linux'` (gui.yml:578), so the unqualified 'the combined-state tests exercise ...' overstates platform coverage for the macOS/Windows rows.

This does not undermine the soft: false decision for the two Linux rows — those ARE covered by the Linux-only combined test — which is why it is minor. But the qualifier should not have been dropped from the sentence that still needs it.
issues.fix_hint:
Restore the qualifier only where it applies:

    #   * The native capability feature set (`hdt,federation,odrl,forms`) is clippied on every
    #     row and each feature is clippied individually by gui.yml's ADVISORY (non-gating)
    #     tauri-build job; the COMBINED-state test runs on the Linux rows only. `custom-protocol`
    #     is exercised only by jobs that first export gui/app/out for compile-time embedding.
issues.title: Unaddressed from round 4: the justification dropped 'on Linux', but the combined-state test is still Linux-only

issues.body:
This PR adds `- name: Test (HDT import, native lane)` running `cargo test --features hdt`. But engine.rs has exactly one hdt-related test, `hdt_import_in_a_lean_build_fails_loudly_with_a_rebuild_hint` (engine.rs:538), and it is `#[cfg(not(feature = "hdt"))]`-gated — so `--features hdt` COMPILES IT OUT and adds no new test at all. The only feature-on hdt code is `load_hdt` (engine.rs:336), which has no test.

So the step is a pure compile check, and it is already fully subsumed by `cargo clippy --all-targets --features hdt` immediately above it (clippy --all-targets compiles the test targets). Net effect: a second full recompile of the hdt permutation on all five rows for zero additional signal, under a name that reads as if HDT import is exercised.

Note this CORRECTS round 4's nit, which claimed the downstream comment 'HDT's feature-on path is compile-covered above' now understates coverage. It does not — that comment is precisely accurate, and should be left alone. The `forms` counterpart is fine: forms.rs:137 and forms.rs:167 are real `#[cfg(feature = "forms")]` tests, so `cargo test --features forms` earns its place.
issues.fix_hint: Either drop the redundant `cargo test --features hdt` step and keep only the hdt clippy lane (the honest framing: hdt is compile-covered, matching release.yml's wording), or rename it to something truthful such as 'Build test targets (hdt dependency edge)'. If real coverage is wanted instead, add a `#[cfg(feature = "hdt")]` test that round-trips a small .hdt fixture through `load_hdt` — then the current step name becomes accurate and release.yml's 'HDT is compile-covered in that feature-on state' should be upgraded to match.
issues.title: 'Test (HDT import, native lane)' runs zero hdt feature-on tests — the step name overclaims and the step is redundant

issues.body:
tauri-build (timeout-minutes: 45, continue-on-error: true) previously ran clippy+build+test on defaults, clippy+test for federation, clippy+test for odrl, plus a Linux-only combined clippy. This PR adds clippy+test for hdt and clippy+test for forms on every row, and removes `if: runner.os == 'Linux'` from the union clippy so it too runs on all five rows.

Each distinct feature set recompiles the whole dependency graph (hdt pulls sparq-hdt, odrl pulls sparq-policy + sparq-solid, forms pulls oxrdf + sparq-forms), so this roughly doubles compile work on macos-15-intel / windows-latest / ubuntu-24.04-arm. On a cold cache that could exceed the 45-minute timeout, and because the job is continue-on-error a timeout is SILENT — so the added coverage may not actually materialise on the slower rows, while release.yml now cites it as evidence.

The redundant hdt test step (previous issue) compounds this. Raised in round 4; unchanged.
issues.fix_hint: Raise `timeout-minutes` for tauri-build, or restore `if: runner.os == 'Linux'` on the union clippy (and consider it for the hdt/forms permutations) so the extra compiles land on the rows whose release counterparts are BLOCKING (soft: false) and where the signal is load-bearing, leaving macOS/Windows on default-feature clippy/build/test.
issues.title: Unaddressed from round 4: union clippy lost its Linux-only guard, adding feature-permutation compiles to a 45-minute advisory job on all five rows

verdict.summary:
No blockers or majors. Verified against the PR-head checkout, not just the diff: all four lean stubs (engine.rs:347, federation.rs:66, odrl.rs:221, forms.rs:89) yield the literal 'rebuild the desktop app with' after Rust line-continuation stripping, so the guard's regex matches every one and a missing feature is caught; productName is "sparq" (tauri-cli renames sparq-gui -> sparq) so the sparq/sparq-gui + .exe loop covers all five rows; the crate has its own [workspace] so gui/src-tauri/target/release is right; no --target is passed, matching the staging step's bundle path; the guard runs BEFORE staging/upload so a contaminated binary cannot ship; grep -q inside an if does not trip set -e; and no frontend/doc string in gui/ or site/ false-positives the regex. custom-protocol is correctly omitted because cargo tauri build appends it itself (Cargo.toml:82-84).

Branch content is UNCHANGED since 'fix: address review round 2' (1392011c) — the only commit since is a conflict-resolution merge — so none of round 4's five findings were addressed; hence stagnant, not regressing. Three carried items stand verbatim: release.yml's step comment self-contradicts (new text says the release enables SHACL-derived forms; the sq-3w29b paragraph 20 lines below still says 'Forms remains opt-in until a release explicitly selects its larger SHACL model stack'); the guard is still negative-only with nothing pinning the sentinel; and the justification still drops 'on Linux' while the combined-state test keeps if: runner.os == 'Linux'.

Two corrections to round 4. (a) Its nit that 'HDT's feature-on path is compile-covered above' understates coverage is wrong in the opposite direction: the only hdt-related test is #[cfg(not(feature = "hdt"))]-gated (engine.rs:538), so the new 'Test (HDT import, native lane)' step runs ZERO hdt feature-on tests. (b) A missed portability risk: the binary grep has no LC_ALL=C, which on BSD grep (the soft macOS rows) can silently fail to match in a UTF-8 locale.
